t: ff.18 Between digital art and AI
st: Why art matters, and how artificial intelligence can be more artistic than humans

sec.t: ff.18.1 Why switching your brain off matters
sec.p: Awe helps us step out of the individual perspective that stays with us most of the time, lightening the weight we give to so many worries. That's the finding of a study in Human Brain Mapping.
Since we've mentioned Duchamp, what better way to bring him back than the ironic exhibition Best Seat in the House by the English collective Rankin?

sec.t: ff.18.3 Art, between artificial intelligence and humans
sec.p: While we're talking about art, where does artificial intelligence fit into all this? Can computers be artists?

sec.t: ff.18.4 Artistic chess: the king of chess
sec.p: Sure, the computer is faster than humans and has a better memory, but in less "repetitive" processes, like creative ones, the machine seems inferior. As Garry Kasparov (beaten at chess by Deep Blue) put it: "I could smell a new kind of intelligence, a very strange kind of…

sec.t: ff.18.5 Paintings recreated by artificial intelligence
sec.p: Even if Artificial Intelligence isn't yet as creative as humans, it can still give us fortissimo extra tools.
